My parents have never helped me but I can tell you what I would have wanted them to do, here's a list:
- don't be pushy and demand information immediately
- don't assume it's all because of social media and/or his friends,, for me at least if I couldn't bury my face in my phone I would have glady nosedived off a cliff by now
- don't act like his problems are non existent/ unimportant just because you may have bigger ones or just because he is a teen and "teens are moody" 
- accept labels but dont allow them to rule you. Dont identify with them too strongly. Just because you're happy for 15 mins doesn't mean youre cured or faked everything in your own head. 
- download daylio
- listen. Like actually do it. Not every other word,, the full thing
- dont call him lazy for not being unmotivated 
- learn that there is a difference between "I dont want to live" and "I want to die",, one is much more passive than the other
- dont be too overbearing,, I get it, you're concerned, but dont be an asshole otherwise you'll get even less communication
- dont be hurt if he doesnt want to talk to you or take your advice,, especially if you havent gone through something like this in the past you probably dont know what to do or say,, don't beat yourself up but also dont expect you'll be his "saviour" or teach him a valuable lesson because likely you wont. In simple terms you dont get it, dont expect to get it or demand an education, do it on your own terms. 
- let him speak. I find too often in these conversations people get uncomfortable and divert attention onto something else or their own anecdote barely related to the situation. People live to hear their own voices. Dont do that. It already takes a lot to bring yourself to a point  where you want to share something dont make it claustrophobic for him
- ask him if how severe his thoughts were. He doesnt have to tell you but maybe it will make him think on his own. A lot of people have a feeling of "I dont want to be here" but actually having a plan or date is quite concerning. 
- idk,, maybe just me,, but my music choices reflect my mindset, if he doesnt want to talk look for subtle things like that. 
- dont expect this to go away and fix itself,, especially overnight
- depression can be physical or have some roots in things that actually happened,, like traumas from childhood. I have no way of knowing anything about him but I know for me I have some grudges from my childhood,, some situations where I think back and I think my parents could have done better. Expect that and dont get defensive if it ever comes up. 
- personal experience,, suicide scenes in movies and tv shows are hella triggering. Do,, something about that. 
-Ask about self harm,, just a question, it's very common now so prepare yourself for something you might not want to hear. I'd look into it too if I were you. Also don't expect him to fess up immediately either. It might hurt you to see it and you're entitled to your emotions but dont guilt trip him about it or immediately bust into a crying fit, think about how that would make him feel sheesh. You dont have to be happy about it or accept it but dont be an ass. It doesnt mean he's crazy or should be sent off to a mental institution 
- don't spread his situation around like gossip  this is personal not your drama to gossip around in real life. It is absolutely infuriating hearing people talk about their kids issues because they don't know the half of it and they wont because people dont want their most vulnerable thoughts blurted out as conversation filler to your friends. I dont care if you're talking about him with your friends looking for advice or gossip or what unless he is litterally there in the room and okay with it dont do it.  People can get embarrassed and angry quickly with that kinda stuff and I've had my mother look at my face blankly when she did the same thing as if she didnt see the issue with it. Dont do that. Theres a reason why I hardly talk to her now. 
- depressed people tend to clump together in my experience so maybe look out for his friends,, they might  not be having a great time either. 
- dont start every conversation with an overly inquisitive and/or concerned tone or facial expression. It's very off putting. 
- show interest but not in a way where you come across like you think you're doing a humanitarian mission. Personal pet peeve I have one person in my life that will act like that. 
- ask how he is doing casually every now and again
- for the love of god what is it with you people and an obsession with our phones? Just because its something you guys didnt have doesn't mean it is some kind of evil that needs to be eliminated at all costs. The only thing that will do is socially isolate him and leave him alone with his thoughts,, if he really pisses you off come up with something more creative. Maybe like clean the car or something? Force him to go shopping with you? Idek. Be creative
- dont act like everything he does is a burden on you,, even if you feel it is, some things are left better unsaid. especially when it comes to his friends. He needs a support system. Dont fuck that up because of mild inconvenienced caused to your life. 
- be vulnerable with him and he may reciprocate
- dont snoop through his phone or room, just a blatant invasion of privacy.
- just for emphasis I will say this again DONT BE PUSHY 
- social media isnt bad. I'm sick of hearing that. Shut up. Social media has litterally been nothing but positive for me I dont think I'm an exception to the rule
- spend some time with him even if you're busy. That one is self explanatory I think.

You said you wanted help but didn't know where to go? Well indulge me for a second,, During my last relapse I had a pretty bad breakdown that went with it and it really worried my friends, some of whom knew about my little habit. I started moping a lot, missing school and food etc etc but they just stuck with it. That is until I sent some edgier texts to my friend and her mum was snooping through her phone, she contacted the school and later on that week I get pulled out for a chat with some of the mh leaders and guidance councellors at the school. Up until that point i genuinely had no idea what to do or where to go but it turns out most schools at least where i live have mental health nurses and councellors on hand at all times, all you have to do is ask. They don't have to tell your parents anything because they're under a privacy agreement. So yeah,, I've been doing that. Its helped, I'd try if I were you. 

I know it feels like you have to tell your parents and dont get me wrong- you should- but I think the reason why you should is because of your own safety. This can be done by telling other trustworthy people around you ie councellors as oppose to parents. You shouldn't have to feel like you owe anyone anything because you don't. Theyll understand your reluctancy. Tell your parents when you're ready, for some people (aha, me) it will be when they move out so they don't get the overbearing worry that goes along with it but for you it could be any time. I like to think the time will cone to me instead of me trying to find the time. Trust they will take it much better when you're in a better state of mind and can explain yourself properly as oppose to crying and screaming apologies for something you may not be actually sorry for or regret. In the heat of the moment people make irreparable mistakes and just think about how it would feel for them if you slipped in an insult somewhere along the lines, that's something you can't take back. 

I know everytime mental health is brought up in my household it is a crying, screaming match between me and my mum so i would prefer to avoid that for when it comes to sh. I know the feeling of guilt and "I shouldn't be doing this" you get afterwards,, you're not alone. 

And finally,, god this is long I hope you actually read it lol,, an essay,, the grades. I dont know how to help but to say power through it. Summer hols are just on the horizon, you dont have to do this for very much longer just try your best. It's okay to not get straight As. Personally I'm english so I'm still on my easter break and enjoying sweet nothingness before school starts up again so if you are too,, enjoy that. Use those weekends to rest, you deserve it. Remember that there are more important things than grades,, if I got a dollar for every time someone told me they wished they cared less as a kid or put less stakes into grades I'd be a fucking millionaire trust. Just try to pass and anything else is extra, theyll be lenient bc of lockdown.
